items.english: "It is nothing else," Tatsuya said with a grin, pressing in. "That riddle I spoke the other day. It is Mitsuyo-sama. You have for the most part guessed, I dare say, what it is I so earnestly desire. Is it agreed? I have taken her."
notes: Kept Mitsuyo-sama per bible. Rendered o-morai moshimashita yo as blunt completed taking, "I have taken her," not a polite request, to keep the demand brutally plain in the same untroubled voice.

items.english: I do not know what happened after this. Tatsuya is said to have lately taken a wife. Who that wife may be. Again, in the depths of a certain study window there is one who would stake the latter half of a lifetime on the study of a great philosophy, and has taken the vexations of worldly experience and cast them away into the midst of a dust heap. Who that person may be. Wind above the reeds, the paulownia left with branches only. Tomorrow, upon whom shall it fall.
notes: Kept both afterlife rumors unresolved: hearsay for the wife, speculation for wife and philosopher, with no gendered pronoun for the philosopher and no identification supplied. Kept the closing seasonal glance as fragment without consolation or moral.

data.say: Drafted the demand and the withheld ending without resolving wife or philosopher.
